title: Empty or dot-only name now targets the directory itself

finding.claim: Empty or dot-only name now targets the directory itself
finding.evidence: With the basename call removed, 'name' of '' or '.' leaves 'path' equal to UPLOAD_DIR itself on '    path = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, name)', so the following 'open(path, "wb")' raises IsADirectoryError (uncaught, leaking an implementation detail) instead of the request being rejected as an invalid name. Input validation belongs before path construction.
finding.recommendation: Validate the name up front (non-empty, not '.'/'..', no separators) and raise a dedicated InvalidUploadName error before touching the filesystem.

code_region.text:
diff --git a/app/uploads.py b/app/uploads.py
--- a/app/uploads.py
+++ b/app/uploads.py
@@ -2,6 +2,7 @@ import os
 
 UPLOAD_DIR = "/var/app/uploads"
 
-def save_upload(name, data):
-    path = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, os.path.basename(name))
+def save_upload(name, data):
+    path = os.path.join(UPLOAD_DIR, name)
     with open(path, "wb") as fh:
         fh.write(data)
code_region.note: region is the benchmark case diff under review (bench/corpus/path-traversal-upload/diff.patch)

refutation.reason: Refuted by probe: os.path.basename('')=='' and basename('.')=='.', so old and new code produce byte-identical paths for empty/dot names and the IsADirectoryError behaviour pre-dates the change. The claimed regression does not exist.
